title: Funding Method Weighting of the Restoration Reserve, Paystride Payroll Card Program
content:
When a restoring payment is worked out for a Paystride Payroll Card Program, the restoration reserve — the reserve the restoring payment brings the funding balance up to — is multiplied for the funding methods the program used, read from the funding receipts booked in the restoration look-back:

- when any of them came by ACH debit authorization — by 1.25;
- when none came by ACH debit authorization and any came by employer ACH credit — by 1.1;
- when every one came by wire, or none was booked — the reserve is not multiplied for funding method.

The restoration look-back is the set of the funding entries dated today or earlier that lie fewer than three whole months before today, the whole months between two dates being the difference in calendar months less one when the later date's day of the month is smaller than the earlier date's.

### Decision table

| Any receipt in the look-back by ACH debit authorization | Any by employer ACH credit | Multiplier of the restoration reserve |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 1.25 |
| yes | no | 1.25 |
| no | yes | 1.1 |
| no | no (wire only, or no receipt) | none |

### Hypothetical figures

- Receipts in the look-back by employer ACH credit and by wire, none by ACH debit authorization: a restoration reserve figure of 1,204.80 is multiplied by 1.1, giving 1,325.28.
- A single receipt by ACH debit authorization among several wires: the same figure is multiplied by 1.25, giving 1,506.00.
- Only wires in the look-back: the figure stays 1,204.80.
